content: The interview process aims to gather insights into the experiences and needs of transgender individuals regarding HIV and other health-related issues. Participants will be asked about various aspects of their lives, including their involvement in the transgender community, experiences with transitioning, sexual health, mental health, and access to HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services. Section 1: Personal Information Participants will be asked about their sources of income, level of English proficiency, current gender identity, sex assigned at birth, sexual orientation, and HIV testing history. They will also be asked about their HIV status and whether they have undergone gender-affirming surgeries. Section 2: HIV Prevention and Knowledge Participants will discuss their knowledge of HIV prevention and their access to related services. They will be asked about their involvement in the transgender community and HIV-related issues, such as through online platforms, community organizations, or health centers. The discussion will also explore their experiences with transitioning, including the age at which they began, the methods they used (e.g., hormone therapy or surgery), and any challenges they faced, such as access to clean needles or medical supervision. Participants will be encouraged to share how transitioning has impacted their lives and whether they encountered any post-operative complications. Section 3: Sexual Health Participants will be asked about their sexual health needs and their use of prevention methods to protect against HIV and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). They will also discuss their access to these prevention tools and, if applicable, their experiences in discordant relationships (where one partner is HIV-positive and the other is not). Section 4: Mental Health and Drug Use The interview will address concerns related to mental health and drug use, including access to clean needles and syringes for injecting hormones, silicone, or recreational drugs. If access to clean needles is a concern, participants will discuss their knowledge of needle and syringe programs (NSP) and opioid substitution therapy (OST). They will also be asked about the availability of clean needles in their community and where they obtain them. Section 5: HIV Testing and Counseling For participants who have been tested for HIV, the interview will explore their experiences with testing, including where they were tested (e.g., public clinics, community-based organizations, private NGOs), whether they went alone or with someone, and how they felt during the process. They will also discuss how they received their results, whether they were referred to HIV treatment and care services, and what they were told about starting ART. Participants will be asked about their knowledge of early treatment initiation and their ideal vision for HIV services. Section 6: They will share their knowledge of these prevention methods, their experiences using them, the perceived benefits, and any challenges they faced. The availability of information about PrEP and PEP in their community will also be discussed. Section 7: Other Health Concerns Participants will have the opportunity to raise any additional health concerns, including co-morbidities such as tuberculosis (TB), hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and other STIs. They can also discuss any other topics or issues they feel are important for the broader transgender community. Debriefing At the end of the interview, participants will be thanked for their time and willingness to share their personal experiences. They will be informed that the data collected will be analyzed, and a report will be written. A copy of the report will be sent to them, likely by early March 2014. Participants will be reminded that no identifying information will be included in the report, and they will be asked if they would like to receive a copy of the report or be contacted for follow-up questions. Participant Information Sheet The World Health Organization (WHO) is conducting these interviews to better understand the HIV-related needs of transgender individuals globally. The study aims to explore risk behaviors, experiences with healthcare services, and the challenges and opportunities for successful HIV prevention, treatment, and care among transgender people. Approximately 20 transgender individuals will participate in this study. Participation in the interview is entirely voluntary. Participants will be asked to provide a phone number or Skype account for the interview, which will last approximately one hour. The interview will be semi-structured, allowing participants to respond freely and discuss topics important to them. The interviews will be voice-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed. Direct quotes may be included in the final report, but no identifying information will be used. Privacy and Confidentiality All information provided by participants will be handled confidentially. A study file with an interview ID number will be created for each participant, and only the interviewer and research team will have access to this file. After the analysis is completed, all personal identifying information and recordings will be deleted. Transcribed interviews will be stored electronically and used in the final report. Published information will not include participants' names or other personal details. Risks and Benefits Participants may feel uncomfortable answering personal questions about their sexual activity, drug use, or transitioning experiences. They are not required to answer any questions they do not wish to and can leave the interview at any time without explanation. There are no direct benefits to participants, but the information gathered will help WHO better understand the needs of transgender individuals and improve HIV prevention, treatment, and care services. Voluntary Participation Participation in the interviews is entirely voluntary. Participants can decline to participate or withdraw at any time without penalty or loss of rights. Questions and Contact Participants are encouraged to ask any questions they may have about the interview process. WHO emphasizes that participation is voluntary and that all information will be kept confidential. This explanation provides a clear and professional summary of the interview process and its purpose, ensuring that participants understand their rights and the importance of their contributions.
